function.mechanism: Provides yellow-orange coloration via curcuminoid chromophore absorption in the visible range; used as a color additive under GMP conditions.

adi.basis: EFSA ANS Panel re-evaluation of curcumin (E100), with ADI retained in later refined exposure context.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA established ADI 3 mg/kg bw/day and indicated possible exceedance in some high-consumption groups, especially children, depending on exposure scenario.

adi.basis: JECFA allocated ADI of 0-3 mg/kg bw based on rat multigeneration NOEL with safety factor 100.

concerns.summary: EFSA identified that high-consumption scenarios may exceed the ADI in children (1-10 years), indicating potential risk management relevance for high-intake subgroups.
Rare human liver injury case reports are associated with concentrated turmeric/curcumin dietary supplements (often with black pepper/piperine), a context distinct from typical food additive exposure.

no_concern_confirmed: A recent genotoxicity safety assessment of a solid lipid curcumin preparation reported no mutagenic/clastogenic signal in the standard test battery at tested doses (PMID: 36609910).
JECFA and EFSA both maintain numerical ADIs (0-3 and 3 mg/kg bw/day respectively), supporting controlled-use safety frameworks.

populations: high consumers in certain exposure scenarios
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA assessments indicate potential ADI exceedance in high-intake scenarios; ordinary use remains regulated by GMP and food-category conditions.

risk_assessment.rationale: E100/curcumin is approved by EFSA, FDA (GRAS context and color additive regulations), and JECFA with established ADIs, but EFSA indicates potential ADI exceedance in some high-consumption subgroups and recent case reports show rare hepatotoxicity with concentrated supplements.
key_factors: US CFR permits turmeric/turmeric oleoresin with GMP and identity restrictions
Potential ADI exceedance in children/high consumers
